critical_evidence.evidence: No borescope images, specialist inspection, or engine rebuild invoice is mentioned for this M97 3.4. The profile treats this as a bonus, but for an S car it is the core due-diligence item to obtain pre-purchase.
No DME over-rev report is provided. Transmission is unstated. If manual, over-rev ranges are essential; if Tiptronic, the report is still useful for runtime and range data.
No receipts for water pump, coolant pipes, AOS, clutch, or major service are listed. The dealer description contains equipment boilerplate only.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is present: VIN with a matching decode, an all-in price including fees, an AutoCheck summary (clean title, 0 accidents, 3 owners), and a photographed Edition 1 numbered plaque. The maintenance half is absent: no receipts, no borescope, no DME report, and no cooling or AOS history. Transmission is not even stated.

condition.rationale: Exterior photos show glossy paint, straight panels, and intact wheels, but nothing proves mechanical condition. There are no underside, engine-bay, tire-date, cluster, or cold-start images. Nothing wrong is stated and nothing is proven.

price_value.rationale: The $31,545 asking price sits just above the top of the $25,417–$31,466 fair-value band (mid $28,072), roughly 12% over mid, for a 71k-mile M97 car with no engine documentation. Edition 1 rarity may carry some premium, but undocumented bore condition offsets it.

mission_fit.rationale: It is plausible as a future keeper, but it is the 3.4 S that the profile says to buy only with unusually strong engine diligence, and none is offered. Transmission is unknown. The price is well above the ideal band and conflicts with the current cash-preservation, bridge-first posture.

logistics.rationale: Everett, WA is far from Carmel but has established Porsche independents nearby for a borescope PPI. Dealer willingness to allow an off-site PPI is unstated. CA smog feasibility depends on the emissions label, which is not shown.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: This is a numbered Porsche Design Edition 1 (580/777) in black with stripes, a genuinely desirable trait. That is held back from 7+ because the transmission is unconfirmed, and a Tiptronic would cut it sharply.

ppi_focus: Borescope all six cylinders (especially 4-6) for scoring; retain the images.
DME over-rev report and engine runtime hours.
Oil analysis and an oil filter cut for metal or plastic debris.
Compression and leakdown, interpreted alongside the borescope.
Smoke on cold start and oil residue in the tailpipes and muffler (bore-scoring and AOS indicators).
Water pump weep, coolant pipe condition, and coolant smell or residue around the expansion tank.
Clutch engagement point and dual-mass flywheel (if manual) or Tiptronic shift quality and fluid condition (if automatic).
Tire dates, alignment wear, and front control arm and bushing condition.
Paint meter across panels and underside inspection for impact or curb damage despite the clean AutoCheck summary.
what_would_change_verdict: Confirmation of a 6-speed manual plus a clean specialist borescope of cylinders 4-6 with images would materially improve condition and fit.
Receipts for water pump, coolant pipes, AOS and clutch would lift documentation and condition.
A Tiptronic confirmation, any scoring on the borescope, or significant over-rev counts in ranges 4+ would move it sharply down.
A price negotiation toward the fair-value midpoint (around $28k) would improve price value.
Dealer refusal of an off-site PPI would push logistics and documentation down.
evidence.mission_note: As a future keeper, a numbered Edition 1 Cayman S is appealing on specification, but it is the 3.4 M97 car the profile says to buy only with unusually strong engine diligence, and none is offered yet. It does not serve the bridge need, and at this price it pulls against the accelerated-bridge cash-preservation strategy.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: VIN [VIN] decodes to a 2008 Cayman S 3.4, a Porsche Design Edition 1 plaque numbered 580/777 is photographed, and the AutoCheck summary shows a clean title, 0 reported accidents and 3 owners. It establishes nothing about mechanical condition: there is no borescope, no DME over-rev report, no cooling, water-pump, AOS or clutch history, and the dealer text is equipment boilerplate. The transmission is not stated at all, which is decisive for Jason's manual preference. Photos show a cosmetically tidy exterior with intact stripes and wheels, but tires, underside and engine bay are not examined here. At $31,545 including fees, the car sits just above the $25,417–$31,466 fair-value band for a 71k-mile M97 without bore evidence. Edition 1 rarity is the main argument for that premium.
evidence.next_action: Call West Coast Auto Works to confirm manual vs Tiptronic and whether an off-site borescope PPI at a Seattle-area Porsche specialist is permitted, and request the full AutoCheck and any service records.
